selected_title: The Hair Clip He Started Carrying
reference_mechanic: Someone is surprised a tiny detail was remembered; the other person treats remembering as obvious.
concept: Aachu reaches for a hair clip right as the food arrives, and Zuv already has her exact old clip in his pocket because he knows this tiny chaos happens every time.
exact_first_slide_text: why do you have my clip?
first_frame_visual: Food has just arrived; Aachu's hair is falling into her face and one hand is already halfway to her bag, while Zuv's hand enters the lower frame holding her old clip.
payoff_frame: Aachu clips her own hair slightly crooked and looks caught between laughing and softening; Zuv has already gone back to eating like this was normal inventory.
share_trigger: Send to the person who carries your tiny emergency object.
comment_trigger: What weird little thing does your person carry/remember for you?
why_it_wins: All three Idea Room agents independently selected the hair-clip direction.
It turns the reference's remembered-detail mechanic into a concrete A Story scene.
The hook is short, raw, and accusation-shaped.
The prop can visually prove the text without a quote-card layout.
The comment bait is specific and natural.
risks: If Aachu does not actually use/lose clips, creator should swap the object before story lock.
Do not stage Zuv fixing Aachu's hair romantically; she should clip it herself.
Do not make Zuv saintly or Aachu helpless.
Do not use the exact reference payoff line.
Do not copy the reference visual style.
